description: Use this when the user wants to know what a YouTube video says or shows: summarise it, find where something is said, check a claim, pull prices or products out of a review. Returns one timeline to read in order: the video's metadata and description, its chapters, the transcript in the language that is spoken (not a translation; you translate if needed) stamped [m:ss], and small frames placed where the speaker points at the screen ('as you can see', 'come vedete'), where a price is said, at each chapter, and every so often in between. Frames are low resolution (usually 160x90): good for seeing the scene and objects, not for reading small text. Long videos: pass start/end to read a part, or max_tokens to bound the text.

end.description: Read up to this point: seconds or 'm:ss'

languages.description: Caption languages to prefer, e.g. ['en']. Leave empty to get the language spoken in the video (recommended: more accurate than a translated track)

max_tokens.description: Token budget for the text part

start.description: Read from this point: seconds or 'm:ss'

url.description: YouTube URL (watch, youtu.be, shorts, embed, live)

name: read_video
